solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some ordinary-looking rising stars

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the run of letters is read from the bottom up, backwards
some of the letters of the following words are taken, a run sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A stargazer notes that a few unremarkable stars are coming up over the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks ARYL from inside 'ordinARY-Looking'; 'rising' turns that run upside down in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyra, the Lyre, is a northern constellation, a group of stars containing Vega.

clue.text: Plan in which the French publicist is seen as incompetent user of language

indicators.note: the plan contains the following pieces, which go inside it
the pieces are shown sitting within the plan

parts.note: a plan of an area is a map
la is the French feminine word for the
a PR man is a pro, short for public relations officer

explanation.surface: A French spin doctor shown up as hopeless with words in some scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Malaprop, from Sheridan's play The Rivals, comically misuses long words; her name gives us malapropism.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Malaprop is the archetype of someone who muddles similar-sounding words, so the name stands for any such bungling speaker.

clue.text: Guys with leader absent in cushy group meeting

indicators.note: the shortened guys go inside the word for cushy

parts.note: a plum job is a cushy, desirable one

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for guys is missing

parts.note: guys are men

explanation.surface: Some men, lacking their boss, have gathered in a comfortable get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenum is a full assembly of all members of a body, a complete gathering.

clue.text: An adjective maybe, one with power in little piece

indicators.note: the pair of letters go inside the word for a little piece

parts.note: a particle is a tiny piece of something
one is the Roman numeral I
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson: an adjective, perhaps, is one with power in a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A participle such as 'broken' often works as an adjective, so the definition gives an example with 'maybe'.

clue.text: Player knowing only seven of his team-mates?

definitions.text: Player knowing only seven of his team-mates?

parts.words: Player knowing only seven of his team-mates?
parts.note: a rugby union player in a half-back position, read as one who has met only half of his fourteen team-mates

explanation.surface: A sports player who has hardly got to know the rest of his side.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union, a side of fifteen, the fly-half is a key back; 'fly' playfully suggests he is acquainted with just half of his fourteen fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby team has fourteen others besides any one player, and seven is half of them, so this player is wryly described by a half.

clue.text: Assault or battle in which nothing is gained

indicators.note: the battle contains what follows
the battle acquires the letter for nothing, taking it inside

parts.note: a fray is a fight or battle
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A pointless attack or fight that wins no ground at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A foray is a sudden raid or attack into enemy territory.

clue.text: Design centres do this to give us hose maybe

parts.words: do this to give us hose
parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: fashion, meaning rework, the word houses and you get the letters of us hose

explanation.surface: Clothes designers turning out stockings and tights for us.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: 'fashion' is the anagram signal applied to HOUSES, which rearranges into US HOSE; 'maybe' marks it as just one possible rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Couture firms such as Dior are the places where clothing designs are created and shown.

clue.text: Drain must be cleaner, not black

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for black is dropped

parts.note: bleach is a household cleaner
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Advice that a plughole needs a cleaning product that is not a dark one.
explanation.definitionFit: To leach is to drain away, as water percolates through soil and carries substances out.

clue.text: Foremost of people to rush violently?

definitions.text: Foremost of people to rush violently?

indicators.note: violently means the letters are thrown about into a new order
only the opening letter of the word people is taken

explanation.surface: Who would be the first person to charge headlong into a fight?
explanation.walkthrough: 'violently' rearranges P with TO RUSH. The whole clue also describes Harry Percy, the impetuous rebel nicknamed Hotspur in Shakespeare's Henry IV.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspur is a rash, hot-headed person, after Shakespeare's impetuous Harry Percy, first to dash into battle.

clue.text: Many ships girl's seen by inlet

indicators.note: the girl appears beside, after, the word for inlet

parts.note: an arm of the sea is an inlet
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is spotted beside a creek where lots of vessels are moored.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, famously the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Leaders in Church Times grounded in good sense and holiness

indicators.note: the two letters are set within, embedded in, the word for good sense

parts.note: sanity is soundness of mind, good sense

indicators.note: the leading letters of Church and Times are taken

explanation.surface: Editorials in a religious newspaper rooted in common sense and piety.
explanation.walkthrough: Church Times is a real Anglican weekly newspaper, which gives the surface its plausibility.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctity is the state of being sacred or saintly, a synonym for holiness.

clue.text: Frightful ado and I cry, wanting mother around to show a bit of heart?

indicators.note: the word for mother goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: mum is mother

indicators.note: frightful suggests a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone wails at a terrible fuss and needs their mother to show some heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightful' is the anagram signal for 'ado' and 'I cry', with 'and' just a link; 'wanting' means needing, so the mother must go 'around' the jumble. The '?' flags that heart is anatomical, not emotional.
explanation.definitionFit: The myocardium is the muscular middle layer of the heart wall, literally a part of the organ.

clue.text: Clerical office involving risks, internal note becoming obvious

indicators.note: the note sits inside the word for risky, and it is that inner letter that changes
becoming means one thing turns into another, the note being swapped

parts.note: chancy means involving risks, risky
plain means obvious, clear

explanation.surface: A church job with hazards, where a memo inside becomes evident.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplaincy is the post or office held by a chaplain, a cleric attached to an institution.

clue.text: Mafia boss caught by a river in Italy

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A gangland leader is arrested beside an Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: A capo is a high-ranking member of a Mafia family, heading a crew.

clue.text: Audibly criticising publication? It may be for present content

definitions.text: It may be for present content

indicators.note: audibly means the word for criticising is taken as heard, its spelling changed

parts.note: rapping means rebuking, criticising sharply
a paper is a newspaper, a publication

explanation.surface: A noisy attack on a newspaper, with talk of what is content now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present content' misleads: present is a gift and content is what fills it, not satisfaction now.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative sheets are used to cover a gift, so they hold the present's contents.

clue.text: Identify and get rid of what sounds like small suspicion

indicators.note: the phrase for small suspicion is said aloud to give the entry

parts.note: a wee doubt is a small suspicion, wee being Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Spot and remove something that seems only a slight misgiving.
explanation.definitionFit: To weed out is to find and eliminate unwanted members or items, as a gardener does.

clue.text: Pain and defeat for optimistic person

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain
a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: Suffering and losing, yet someone still looks on the bright side.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Pangloss is the relentlessly optimistic tutor in Voltaire's Candide.
explanation.definitionFit: Voltaire's tutor believes all is for the best, so his name stands for any blind optimist.

clue.text: Cruel chap ditching old wife

indicators.note: ditching means discarding, so these letters leave the word for chap

parts.note: a fellow is a chap
O is old and W is wife, both standard abbreviations

explanation.surface: A heartless man leaves his former spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell as an adjective means fierce or savage, as in 'one fell swoop'.

clue.text: China's top sporting event

parts.note: the crown is the top of the head or of a hat
a derby is a horse race or a local sports match

explanation.surface: A claim that a Chinese contest is the best there is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is porcelain, not the country. Crown Derby is a famous English porcelain made in Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Crown Derby is a long-established English porcelain maker, so its ware is an example of fine tableware.

clue.text: An example of one could be 'made up' in crosswords!

definitions.text: An example of one could be 'made up' in crosswords!

parts.words: An example of one could be 'made up' in crosswords!
parts.note: in a down clue 'made up' would mean EDAM read upwards, and Edam is a Dutch dairy product of this kind

explanation.surface: A comment that crossword clues are often invented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' in a down clue reverses, so 'made up' gives EDAM, a type of this food.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a well-known variety, so a crossword's 'made up' really names one kind of this dairy food.

clue.text: Mark shows animal has lost its tail

indicators.note: the last letter of the animal's name is removed

parts.note: a badger is a burrowing animal

explanation.surface: A sign that a creature has had its tail docked.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is an emblem or distinguishing sign, a mark of membership or office.

clue.text: Number being entertained by employer — not what you'd get with a fat cat!

definitions.text: not what you'd get with a fat cat!

indicators.note: being entertained means being hosted inside, so the number goes within the employer

parts.note: a boss is an employer
nine is a number

explanation.surface: A number of staff wined and dined by a wealthy boss, who is no fat cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat cat' suggests a rich executive, but read literally a fat cat is plump, the opposite of bony.
explanation.definitionFit: A plump animal has no visible bones, so skinniness is the opposite of its condition.

clue.text: Not one of our characters to slate the dental establishment

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or criticise, as slate means to censure
BDA is the British Dental Association

explanation.surface: Someone foreign sets out to attack the dentists' professional body.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is a letter of the Greek alphabet, not one of the Roman letters English uses.

clue.text: Important location for 9

definitions.meaning: the Spanish ..., an old name for the sea of the Caribbean, where great fleets sailed, the fleet of 9

explanation.surface: Somewhere significant for the fleet in 9.
explanation.definitionFit: Main is an adjective for principal and an old noun for the open sea, where ships sail.

clue.text: Volunteers coming with lettuce and Mexican food

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
cos is a long-leaved variety of lettuce

explanation.surface: Volunteers arrive with salad and a Mexican meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacos are folded tortillas with a filling, a staple Mexican dish.

clue.text: Sigh as American grabbed by one of Oxford's prominent features?

indicators.note: the American letters are seized and held inside the feature

parts.note: Oxford is the city of dreaming spires, so a spire is one of its prominent features
US is the United States, American

explanation.surface: An American visitor caught up in an Oxford landmark heaves a sigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspire is a literary verb meaning to breathe out heavily, to sigh.
